AGENDA
  GLENDALE ARTS AND CULTURE COMMISSION
  COUNCIL CHAMBER, City Hall – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
Welcome to Glendale City Hall. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast
throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for
purchase in the City Clerk’s Office. Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at
http://www.glendaleca.gov/government/agendas-minutes. If you have any question about matters on the
agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business
hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language
translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices are available same-day
upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign language
translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that
are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the
Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who wish to utilize
the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City Clerk’s office at 818-548-
2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify the language for which you require
translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their
own interpreter or speak in their native language.

  JULY 18, 2019
  1. ROLL CALL
  a. Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the July 18, 2019
  Regular Meeting was Posted on July 12, 2019 on the Bulletin Board Outside City
  Hall.
  2. CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
  Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  a. Minutes of the Regular Arts and Culture Commission Meeting of May 16, 2019
  b. Minutes of the Special Arts and Culture Commission Meeting of May 16, 2019

  3. INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS
  a. Gary Shaffer, Director - Library Arts & Culture – New staff introduction
  b. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Chuck Wike, Community Relations
  Manager.

  4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5
  Minutes. Members of the Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the
  Speaker, but there will be no Debate or Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff
  Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.

  5. BUSINESS AGENDA
   A. ACTION ITEM(s)
  a. Report regarding Glendale Arts Open Arts & Music Festival co-sponsorship
  opportunity and temporary art installation.
  i. Motion for the Arts & Culture Commission’s co-sponsorship and funding a
  temporary public art installation from the 2019-2020 Work Plan.

  b. Report regarding Redesign of the Art & Entertainment District on Artsakh Avenue
  and nearby alley
  ii) Motion to note and file.

  B. INFORMATION ITEM(s)

  C. DISCUSSION ITEM(s)
  a. 2019-2020 Work Plan Progress
  i.  CITY-WIDE ARTS
  a. Beyond the Box
  ii.  NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS
  a. Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station
  b. Word On The Street
  iii.  PERFORMING ARTS
  iv.  WEBSITE UPDATE
  v.  SPENDING TO DATE

6. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
7. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS
8. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission is August 16, 2019, at 2:00
  p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor.

CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Regular Meeting

  Thursday, July 18, 2019 at 2:00 p.m.
1. ROLLCALL
  • The meeting was called to order on July 18, 2019 at 2:01 p.m.
  • Present: Commissioners Oshagan, Tufenkian, Chairperson Vidor
  • Absent: Vice Chair Zadorian
  • The Agenda for the July 18, 2019 Regular Meeting was Posted on Monday, July 15, 2019 on the
  Bulletin Board Outside City Hall.

2. CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  A. Approval of Regular Meeting Minutes from May 16, 2019

  Moved:  Commissioner Oshagan
  Seconded:  Commissioner Tufenkian
  A roll call was conducted and the Commissioners voted as follows:
  Ayes:  Commissioners Oshagan, Tufenkian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Vice Chair Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

  B.  Approval of Special Meeting Minutes from May 16, 2019 - Approved as Amended

  Moved:  Commissioner Oshagan
  Seconded:  Commissioner Tufenkian
  A roll call was conducted and the Commissioners voted as follows:
  Ayes:  Commissioners Oshagan, Tufenkian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Vice Chair Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

3. INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS
  A. Gary Shaffer, Director - Library Arts & Culture - New Staff introduction
  • Announced the new Arts and Culture Administrator, Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, formerly with Arts
  for L.A. Director Shaffer invited Ms. Fukitomi-Jones to the dais where she introduced herself.
  B. Library, Arts & Culture Events - Presented by Chuck Wike, Community Relations Manager
  • Mr. Wike gave an overview of current and upcoming events at Glendale Library, Arts & Culture
  locations.
 4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Speaker(s):
  Jennifer Hiramoto, Deputy Director of Economic Development:
  o Ms. Hiramoto spoke about City of Glendale - Techweek scheduled for September 14th through
  September 21 51 . More information can be found at www.glendaletechweek.com
  o Ms. Hiromoto stated that this year, Techweek will be comprised of 50 pop up events hosted by
  community groups, schools, the city of Glendale and possibly local artists. She stated local artists,
  referred by Brand Library, Lora Darlington and Selwa Sweidan will be seeking financial support and
  will be coming to the Commission in August to ask for funding for a project during Techweek
  involving pioneering female artists and technologists from local institutions and labs. Economic
  Development has offered a $500 cash contribution and gallery space on Arsakh towards project.
  Director Shaffer suggested bringing back the discussion as an item on next month's agenda. Chair
  Vidor agreed to bring it back as an action item.

5. BUSINESS AGENDA
  A. ACTION ITEM(s)
  a. Report regarding Glendale Arts Open Arts & Music Festival co-sponsorship opportunity and
  temporary art installation.
  i.)  Motion for the Arts and Culture Commission's co-sponsorship and funding a temporary
  public art installation from the 2019-2020 Work Plan.
  •  Mr. Wike gave a brief summary of the Open Arts and Music Festival co-sponsorship
  opportunity and funding.
  •  Jennifer Granville, Special Events Manager at Glendale Arts requested consideration for
  Commission funding of a temporary public art piece at the Open Arts & Music festival on
  September 14, 2019. Ms. Granville gave a brief summary of what the Open Arts &
  Musical Festival will entail and invited the Commission to be part of the selection
  process to choose the artist, share the opportunity with artists and attend the festival.
  •  Commissioner Tufenkian asked if an artist was already selected, about the location of
  the art piece and how long the art piece would stay on location. Ms. Granville stated that
  the artist has not been selected and the art piece would be placed on the festival
  grounds, northwest comer of Brand Blvd, near California. Ms. Granville stated it will be a
  one day installation, duration of the festival.
  •  Commissioner Oshagan suggested the Call for Artists be made proposing that a tech-
  artist be the best fit for the temporary art installation.
  •  Chair Vidor suggested the Call for Artists come from the Arts and Culture Commission
  with the cooperation of the other two organizations. Director Shaffer suggested it be a
  collaborative effort. Ms. Granville agreed.
  •  Chair Vidor asked that once the Call for Artists is out, how will the collaborate decision
  making of choosing an artist and collaborate decision making on where the art piece will
  be relocated happen. She also suggested the art installation stay longer than a day at
  its first location, then relocate it elsewhere per the Commission's direction and stated
  relocation of art piece should be indicated in the Call for Artists.
  •  Commissioner Oshagan stated the kind of art will determine if it can be relocated but
  there needs to be a plan set in place to decide if it will be relocated and where it will go.
  •  Commissioner Tufenkian suggested relocating the art piece in one place so it's cost
  effective.
  •  Director Shaffer stated it would be collaboration between staff and the Commission on
  the relocation site of the art piece and also stated bringing the cost for relocation of the
  temporary art installation back as an item to next month's meeting.

  2
   Motion that the Arts & Culture Commission hereby:
  1.  Co-sponsor the 2019 Glendale Arts Open Arts & Music Festival;
  2.  Fund a temporary public art installation at the Open Arts & Music Festival in the
  amount of $5,000 from the 2019-2020 Work Plan; and
  3.  Direct staff to modify and execute the "call to artists" for such temporary public art
  installation in collaboration with and with input from Glendale Arts, consistent with
  the comments and the direction provided by the Commission at the July 18, 2019
  meeting.

  Moved:  Commissioner Oshagan
  Seconded: Commissioner Tufenkian
  A roll call was conducted and the Commissioners voted as follows :
  Ayes:  Commissioners Oshagan, Tufenkian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Vice Chair Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

  b.  Report regarding Redesign of the Arts & Entertainment District on Artsakh Avenue and nearby
  alley.
  ii.)  Motion to note and file .

  •  Mr. Wike gave a brief summary of report regarding the redesign of the Arts and
  Entertainment District.
  •  Jennifer Hiramoto, Deputy Director of Economic Development and Shannon Heffernan,
  Urban Design Director at Studio One Eleven gave a detailed PowerPoint presentation
  regarding the redesign of the Arts & Entertainment District on Artsahk Avenue and
  nearby alley.
  •  Tamara O'Conner of Studio Eleven and Community Arts Resources asked the
  Commission to identify three options including Gateway signage, Iconic Art and
  seasonal/rotating art from a list provided via PowerPoint presentation so that their ideas
  may be incorporated into the project and Economic Development can work with the
  Commission's intentions in mind. Commission chose as followed:
  o Commission Tufenkian: Gateway signage, Iconic Sculpture and benches
  o Commission Oshagan: Gateway signage, Interactive/participatory art,
  canopy/shade structures, tech art, iconic permanent art piece
  o Chair Vidor: Thematic gateway signage, street color, patterns, wall art

  Motion that the Director of Library, Arts & Culture's July 18, 2019 report regarding the
  redesign of the Art & Entertainment District on Artsakh A venue, is hereby received,
  noted and filed.

  Moved:  Commissioner Tufenkian
  Seconded: Commissioner Oshagan
  A roll call was conducted and the Commissioners voted as follows:
  Ayes:  Commissioners Oshagan, Tufenkian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Vice Chair Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

B. INFORMATIONAL ITEM(s)
  •  There are no items.

  3
   C. DISCUSSION ITEM (s)
  a. 2019-2020 Work Plan Progress
  •  Mr. Wike provided a brief update on the Work Plan progress and programs that have had
  recent activity.
  i. City Wide Arts
  a. Beyond the Box
  Staff is planning a new phase of utility box murals and also contacted art instructors at
  Glendale high school so that students can submit for utility boxes located directly in front
  of the high school.
  b. Artwalk
  Staff is working with the legal department to prepare and issue a Request for Proposal
  (RFP} for an Event Management Consultant to plan and execute a pilot Glendale Art
  Walk event.
  ii. Neighborhood Arts
  a. Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station
  Staff has received eighteen applications to exhibit art in the Adams Square Mini Park
  Gas Station. Staff is working with the Arts and Culture Commission's selection
  committee to schedule a review of the applications.
  b. Word on the Street
  Legal department completed an artist agreement with Scott Froschauer. Staff will work
  with Community Services & Parks and Traffic and Transportation and the artists to install
  eighteen signs. Staff is also working with Mr. Froschauer on a sign outside of the
  Downtown Central library. This sign is called GROW.
  iii. Performing Arts
  The popular Brand Plaza series and the 222 EAST series continue through the month of
  August.
  iv. Website Update
  Staff is working with a web developer to produce an Arts and Culture Commission
  website.
  v. Spending To Date
  To date $19,000 of funds set aside for the 2019-2020 Work Plan have been spent and an
  additional $26,250 has been encumbered.

6. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
  •  Chair Vidor thanked Library, Arts & Culture for having a Library volunteer recognition event.
  She also inquired about the chess pieces that were part of a chess park in Glendale;
  Director Shaffer inquired as to whether they were funded by the Arts & Culture
  Commission. Chair Vidor said they were not. Director Shaffer
  stated he would make some inquiries and report back.

7. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS
  •  None

8. ADJOURNMENT - 3:49 p.m.

  The next regular meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission is August 15, 2019, at 2:00 p.m. in the City
  Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor.
